cohort: 469 twin pregnancies (dichorionic or monochorionic-diamniotic) between 24 and 36 weeks of gestation admitted for preterm labor at a single tertiary center between 2011 and 2018
finding: While cesarean delivery shortened the latency period, it increased the risk of respiratory distress syndrome when accounting for gestational age at preterm labor presentation.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery shortened the latency period between preterm labor presentation and actual delivery, but was associated with an increased risk of respiratory distress syndrome after adjusting for gestational age at preterm labor presentation.
